title: Sulfur-bearing molecules in a sample of early star-forming cores
question: How do abundances of sulfur-bearing molecules (34SO, SO2, NS, SO, SO+, H2CS) relate to gas temperature, column density and line widths in early star-forming cores?

evidence.quote: for which we adopt the value of 0.0185 cm$^2$g$^{-1}$ (cite: csengeri2017)

what.value: Molecular line parameters (Eu, gu, Aul, Q) from Splatalogue/CDMS

evidence.quote: Note: Parameters extracted from the Splatalogue Database for

what.value: Cloud distances and v_LSR from catalogs

evidence.quote: Distances were obtained from the catalogs in Vizier ‘ATLASGAL cold high-mass clumps with NH$_{3}$’ (cite: wie12)

recipe.method: Cores identified in 0.87 mm continuum; most intense core per clump; spectra extracted at continuum peak with a beam-size circular region
Gaussian fits to each line for peak, FWHM and integrated flux W; only main component fitted when wings present
Upper-level column density from W, Aul and beam area, then total column density using partition function
assumptions: Tex = 20 K for all lines and cores; optically thin

recipe.method: Rotational diagram from two CH3OH lines, Trot taken as Tkin
assumptions: LTE, optically thin, beam filling factor 1

recipe.goal: Derive N(H2), mass and density from continuum
recipe.method: Kauffmann et al. 2008 formulae with beam-integrated 0.87 mm flux; density from sphere of beam diameter
assumptions: kappa = 0.0185 cm2/g at 870 um; Tdust = Tkin

recipe.method: X = N/N(H2); linear fits with R2 of X vs T, X vs N, X vs X; line width histograms and Pearson coefficients

evidence.quote: We obtain a media of 1.6, with a maximum value of 9.29 and a minimum of 0.06.
The average measured temperature of our sample is 65 K.

answer_key.quantity: Pearson coefficients of X vs X(SO) for SO+, NS, SO2, H2CS

evidence.quote: for such abundance relations are 0.83, 0.87, 0.93, and 0.93, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Pearson correlation of H2CS and NS line widths

evidence.quote: there is an excellent correlation between H$_2$CS and NS ($\rho = 0.93$)
